You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

await rlm.harness.create_memory(
    key='arc_task_f2eb5109_verified_snake_rule_and_anomalous_test',
    content='ARC task-f2eb5109. Four demos verify: preserve the background, full horizontal barrier rows, and the two side cells of each 3-cell gate. Draw a one-cell-wide orthogonal snake in the endpoint/marker color, starting at the upper isolated marker, visiting gate centers in top-to-bottom barrier order, then ending at the lower isolated marker. For each gate, descend at the previous column to the row immediately above that gate, draw horizontally to its center column, recolor only the center gate cell to the path color, and continue. After the last gate, descend to the lower endpoint row and draw horizontally to that endpoint. Demos had path/endpoint colors 2,4,6,3. ANOMALOUS UNSOLVED TEST: 30x30 background 5; endpoints 1 at zero-based (1,9),(28,11); orange 7 rows r=4,7,15 with yellow 4 gates at (r4,c15..17), (r7,c4..6), (r15,c20..22). The direct demo-derived blue path was rejected. Its turns were r3 c9..16, r6 c5..16, r14 c5..21, r27 c11..21; verticals c9 r1..3, c16 r4..6, c5 r7..14, c21 r15..27; gate centers recolored 1. Also rejected: same geometry with red 2 path and blue endpoints; all-red path/endpoints; yellow 4 path with blue endpoints; all-yellow path/endpoints; blue path with yellow 4 endpoints; blue path with all gate centers left yellow. Do not repeat these eight outputs. Four demos requested; instance reached 8/8 wrong.',
    metadata={'task_id':'task-f2eb5109','status':'rule_verified_but_test_unsolved'},
    global_=True
)
